profile.name: Mei-Ling Chao
profile.subline: New-grad fintech and data science roles for a June 2027 graduate · Tailored to your September 2026 resume
profile.recentRole: RBC Capital Markets — Quant Strategies Intern
profile.stack: Python, SQL, R, Excel, Bloomberg Terminal
profile.target: New Grad FT · Toronto / Remote-Canada · Fintech + Data
profile.summary: Two brand-name Canadian internships, RBC on the quant side and Shopify on the data side, put you ahead of most commerce graduates; lead with the Python strategy work rather than the coursework. The important constraint on this board is legal, not technical: most of these employers hire into the United States and would need to sponsor you, so the Canadian employers in the suggested list are the realistic core of your search.
profile.applyNow: None of the live roles on this board hire into Canada without sponsorship. Start with **RBC's graduate program** and **Shopify**, where you already have internal history.
profile.watchLater: The Big Five bank campus programs all open their fall windows between September and November; Wealthsimple and Cohere post irregularly, so set alerts rather than waiting.

suggested.name: RBC (Royal Bank of Canada)
suggested.why: **You already interned here, which beats every other advantage on this board.** The quant strategies work in Python is exactly what RBC's graduate analytics programs recruit for; ask your manager about the return-offer path first.
suggested.note: Runs a formal Graduate Program and Amplify internship with fall application windows; apply through jobs.rbc.com.

suggested.name: Shopify
suggested.why: **Your second internship, and a rare Canadian company with genuine data scale.** Reconnect with the data team you worked with before their Dev Degree and new-grad cycles open.
suggested.note: Hires new grads into data and engineering roles; watch shopify.com/careers for 'Data Scientist' and early-career postings.

suggested.name: Cohere
suggested.why: **Toronto's flagship AI lab.** A finance-and-economics background is unusual there, so lead with the Python quant work rather than the commerce degree.
suggested.note: Small and competitive; postings appear on cohere.com/careers with occasional new-grad and residency openings.

suggested.name: Wealthsimple
suggested.why: **The Canadian fintech that best matches your RBC quant experience.** Investing products mean the data work stays close to markets.
suggested.note: Posts analyst and associate roles on wealthsimple.com/careers; hiring is Toronto-centric with hybrid arrangements.

suggested.name: TD Bank Group
suggested.why: **Large Toronto bank with a structured graduate intake.** Reliable rather than exciting, and a strong fallback next to RBC.
suggested.note: Runs a Graduate Leadership Program with fall deadlines; apply at td.com/careers.

suggested.name: Scotiabank
suggested.why: **Another Big Five bank hiring finance-plus-data analysts.** Their analytics teams take commerce grads who can code, which describes you.
suggested.note: Hires through a Campus Program with fall application windows; search 'Analyst' on scotiabank.com/careers.

suggested.name: BMO
suggested.why: **Standard Big Five graduate pipeline.** Worth an application in the same batch as TD and Scotiabank.
suggested.note: Campus recruitment runs in the fall; look for 'Analyst, Capital Markets' and data analyst postings.

suggested.name: CIBC
suggested.why: **Completes the Big Five set.** Applying to all of them in one sitting costs you little and raises your odds materially.
suggested.note: Fall campus program with rotational analyst roles; apply at cibc.com/campus.

suggested.name: Manulife
suggested.why: **Insurance analytics, which is closer to your risk coursework than it sounds.** Less competitive than the banks.
suggested.note: Runs a Global Analyst Program; search manulife.com/careers for early-career postings.

suggested.name: Sun Life
suggested.why: **Another insurer with a real actuarial and analytics pipeline.** A sensible diversification away from banking.
suggested.note: Hires new grads into analyst roles; check sunlife.com/careers in the fall.

suggested.name: Questrade
suggested.why: **Smaller Canadian brokerage.** Fewer seats, but the work is closer to markets than a bank's back office.
suggested.note: Occasional analyst postings on questrade.com/careers; no formal program.

suggested.name: Vector Institute
suggested.why: **Toronto's AI research institute.** Mostly a route to research-adjacent roles and a network rather than a direct new-grad employer.
suggested.note: Runs internships and a postgraduate affiliate program; see vectorinstitute.ai/careers.
